messages:
maria: FYI noticed a ~2x tail latency regression on short sequences after the adaptive-kernel-selector rollout at 2178001000. P99 up from 48ms -> ~95ms on mini-bench.
sam: hmm, any flamegraphs or nsys captures? could be batching or a kernel choice regression.
maria: uploaded two captures to CI (links below). Quick notes: burst of tiny kernel launches around the same time as a spike in cudaMemcpy calls. KV cache hit rate looked normal.
raj: sounds like launch density increased. did the selector start preferring small-fused kernels? that can increase launch overhead + more host<->device traffic if we changed prefetching.
maria: exact command used for nsys (ran on a repro run):
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --output=batch-spike-2178 \
  --sample=none --capture-range=nvtx --nvtx-threads=all \
  -- ./run_minibatch --seq-len=32 --batch=1 --model=redwood-small
```
maria: attached snippet from the timeline (cropped):
```
[time 00:01:23.450] kernel_launch A.size=64  0.12ms
[time 00:01:23.460] cudaMemcpyAsync H2D  0.35ms
[time 00:01:23.480] kernel_launch B.size=8   0.08ms
[time 00:01:23.482] cudaMemcpyAsync H2D  0.33ms
```
jen: is this the change that landed in commit 8f3a2c? that PR adjusted the batching heuristic to prefer lower-latency kernel variants for short context.
sam: yes, 8f3a2c updated the kernel score to penalize memory footprint less. Could cause more small-kernel probes.
raj: if kernels are smaller, kernel-launch overhead + memcpy churn can dominate. need to compare before/after selection counts.
perf-bot: artifact uploaded: https://ci.internal/redwood/nsys/artifacts/batch-spike-2178.nsys [view]
deploy-bot: rollout of adaptive-kernel-selector v2 at 2178001000 -> success :white_check_mark:
maria: I diffed launch counts: before (ref 2177999000) small-kernel launches 180 -> after 460 over same workload window.
sam: that's a huge shift. can you run a focused trace with kernel selection logging enabled? e.g., set KERNEL_DEBUG=1 and run the same nsys capture.
maria: running now. also will bisect between 2177995000..2178001000 if we confirm it's behavioral not env.
jen: suggest capturing one run with the old selector config (pin env KERNEL_SEL_OVERRIDE=legacy) and one with new, to isolate runtime vs commit.
aria: (typo) I meant maria :)
raj: for the bisect, check both the selection table and KV cache eviction timings. small kernels may cause more KV writes/evictions if prefetch window changed.
maria: new capture with KERNEL_DEBUG produced this small log (excerpt):
```
[selector] chosen_variant=V_small score=0.62 reason=latency_pref
[selector] chosen_variant=V_small score=0.61 reason=latency_pref
[cache] prefetch: key=blk_123 evict=0
```
maria: initial bisect candidate commit that flips the heuristic: 8f3a2c -> will run bisect jobs across the commit range and share nsys links.
sam: also instrument kernel launch batching: group launches within 200us as one event; we might be seeing serialized launches due to host-side scheduling.
jen: could be CPU-side hot loop now, tethering launches. capture CPU stack samples too (nsys cpuSampling) so we can see host thread stalls.
perf-bot: bisect job scheduled: https://ci.internal/redwood/bisect/2178003456 (jobs queued)
maria: quick before/after numbers from microbench (median per-token latency): before=12.4ms, after=18.9ms. tail moves more.
raj: OK plan: (1) run `nsys` with cpu sampling + nvtx for five runs old vs new; (2) collect kernel selection logs; (3) check KV cache metrics for increased memcopies; (4) if confirmed, revert selector change or add a launch-coalescing pass.
sam: agreed. i can add a short diff that increases launch coalescing window to see if it mitigates.
maria: thanks — will post artifacts once bisect finishes. tagging @sam @raj for visibility. :eyes:
perf-bot: bisect step 1 finished, candidate bad commit: 8f3a2c -> trace: https://ci.internal/redwood/nsys/bisect/2178003456/step1.nsys
jen: nice, once we have the full bisect stack we can decide whether to tune heuristic or adjust runtime batching.
sam: if we end up needing a quick patch, prefer runtime coalescing in the serving runtime so it helps all variants.
maria: noted. logging final: will follow up with short PR if bisect confirms. thanks all. :pray:
